To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
minimally invasive plate osteosynthesis with titanium locking plates is a viable alternative for the treatment of distal tibia fractures.
minimally invasive medial plate osteosynthesis of distal tibia fractures with locking plates resulted in delayed secondary healing compared to nonlocking plates.
minimally invasive medial distal tibia plating with titanium plates is a safe and efficient technique for the treatment of extra-articular fractures of the distals tibia.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a new method for the treatment of the distal fractures of the tibia.
the development of a new type of a locking plate, a titanium locking plate for the treatment of extra-articular distal tibiofibular fractures.
the development of an innovative method for the treatment of fractures in the distal third of the tibia.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the use of locking plates for distal tibias fractures is associated with a higher rate of delayed union and nonunion compared to the use of non-locking plates.
the titanium locking plate is a more stable fixation device for minimally invasive medial fixation of distal metaphyseal tibia fractures.
in the biological fixation of distals tibial fractures with a minimally invasive approach, similarly good results can be obtained with either stainless steel non-locking or titanium locking plates.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we found no difference in clinical outcomes of minimally invasive medial plate fixation of extra-articular distal tibias with either a nonlocking stainless steel or a titanium locking plates.
minimally invasive plating with titanium plates and screws in the treatment of distal tibia fractures is associated with prolonged healing times compared to stainless steel plates and screws.
in biological fixation for distal tibias, locking technology has a greater effect on the stability of the construct than the material of the implant.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the locking technology has a greater effect on the stability of the construct than the material used.

titanium locking plates provide a good alternative to conventional nonlocking plates for the fixation of distal extra-articular tibial metaphyseal and intra-articular distal tibiofibular joint fractures.
